key_insight: Video Streaming Thinking (VST) lets VideoLLMs 'think while watching' by running a reasoning stream concurrently with the visual perception stream, dramatically reducing response latency without degrading logical reasoning quality.
problem_solved: Addresses the trade-off in online VideoLLMs where enabling synchronized logical reasoning during streaming raises unacceptable test-time latency; enables timely, coherent reasoning during live video input.
method: Dual-stream paradigm: decouples continuous visual encoding (watching) from the logical inference pipeline (thinking) so both run concurrently and asynchronously.
Incremental reasoning: activates reasoning on partial/accumulated visual features and uses context caching to start inference early rather than waiting for full frames or long buffers.
Latency-aware synchronization: lightweight synchronization and test-time scaling strategies (progressive context aggregation and selective compute) balance responsiveness and reasoning accuracy.
impact: Makes VideoLLMs viable for real-time interactive applications (live QA, robot perception, surveillance) by reducing response latency while retaining robust multimodal reasoning—easing deployment and improving user experience.

paper_title: Video Streaming Thinking: VideoLLMs Can Watch and Think Simultaneously
paper_authors: Yiran Guan, Liang Yin, Dingkang Liang, Jianzhong Ju, Zhenbo Luo
